text:
anya: quick thread — we keep bikeshedding prefetch vs debounce heuristics for paginated endpoints. propose a small, language-agnostic surface: `prefetch_count`, `debounce_ms`, and `prefetch_strategy: [eager|lazy|adaptive]`. thoughts?

mike: +1 for small surface. adaptive is the tricky bit though — needs runtime telemetry to avoid oscillation.

talia: can we avoid exposing `debounce_ms` in python? it's an event-loop detail and feels different between py/ts/go. maybe `debounce_ms` only in ts, `debounce` bool in py/go? :thinking_face: 

sandeep: i'd rather keep parity. devs expect the same knobs across SDKs. hide implementation differences behind sane defaults, but expose values for advanced users.

kevin: ergonomics: default `prefetch_count=1` and `adaptive` off. `adaptive` enables an internal EWMA of latency and throughput and increases prefetch up to N. Implementation sketch: ```js
// pseudo
if (strategy === 'adaptive') {
  window.update(latency, success);
  prefetch = min(max_prefetch, baseline * (1 + util_factor));
}
```

anya: +1 for sane defaults. question: how do retries interact with prefetch? we don't want duplicate downstream requests or double-charges.

olga: retries should be per-item idempotent if possible. Add an optional `idempotency_key` per page request; if not provided, we stay conservative and disable overlapping prefetch + retry collision by ensuring only one inflight request per cursor token.

mike: that idempotency_key idea is good. but for streaming endpoints we may need different approach — resumable cursors vs page tokens. we should document recommended patterns.

anya: doc + SDK behavior: propose docs say "use idempotency_key for aggressive prefetch + retries; otherwise SDK will serialize prefetch when retrying".

kevin: cross-lang surface: expose `prefetch_count` (int), `strategy` (string), `max_prefetch` (int), `enable_debounce` (bool), and `debounce_ms` (int). languages that can't do ms precision can accept ms rounded to 100ms.

mike: TS: `debounce_ms` sensible default 50ms. Py: default keep 0 and rely on `asyncio` scheduling + batch window. Go: 10ms. These can be platform defaults but same keys.

talia: concern: adding too many knobs makes QA matrix explode. can we hide `enable_debounce` behind an `auto_tune` flag that flips on/off both debounce and adaptive?

anya: that may be OK. `auto_tune` (bool) + `advanced` object (advanced only shown in docs). But remember agents.md — keep surface small. maybe `auto_tune` + explicit `advanced` should be behind an opt-in builder API.

mike: +1. builder API like: `client.pager().withAutoTune(true).withMaxPrefetch(4)` so defaults remain simple.

olga: noted: need to update rollout plan. start behind feature flag on hosted, then enable in dedicated customers opt-in, run e2e perf tests.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: perf/telemetry-featureflag -> canary 5% at 2024-11-06T18:00Z :rocket:

anya: action items: 1) write short RFC addendum with surface names & defaults (anya) 2) implement thin shim in ts + py + go that accept keys but map to platform defaults (mike/kevin) 3) add idempotency_key support in pager request (olga/sandeep) 4) telemetry hook for adaptive (kevin) 5) docs + examples with patterns and warnings (talia). I'll drop a draft RFC later today.

mike: thanks — I'll start a minimal TS impl and push a prototype branch.

sandeep: I'll sketch the idempotency_key wire format and the serverside expectations in the RFC.

anya: thanks team :heart:
